text:
taylor: apac-prod (apac-a) GPU pools are showing a huge latency spike after the runtime push at 15:01 UTC. 99p went from ~40ms -> ~420ms. KV cache hit rate collapsed from 92% -> 34%. Not seeing available spare GPUs in APAC.
jeff: which deploy/tag? any obvious errors in logs?
sandeep: that was runtime v1.3.7 — I flipped kernel-selection heuristics and enabled continuous batching tweaks at 15:01. I’m seeing a new eviction pattern: prefix cache TTLs are shorter and many KVs are being evicted immediately.
li: we don't have capacity to hot-add GPUs in apac — all pools ~95% utilized. We can shift traffic to na1 but cross-region will add ~60-120ms tail latency for some customers.
taylor: can we hot-disable continuous batching for apac? seems like batching blew up batch size for long seqs -> huge scheduling delay.
maya: oncall, can we rollback? This is affecting production customers.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback request received for runtime v1.3.7 -> v1.3.6 by sandeep. Initiating canary -> global rollback.
jeff: while rollback is in progress, recommend forcing small batches and turning off dynamic kernel fallback on APAC. Patch config will be minimal.
sandeep: ack. applying emergency flags now.
jeff: run this on apac-config-store:
```
PATCH /config/runtime/apac
{ "CONTINUOUS_BATCHING_ENABLED": false, "MAX_BATCH_SIZE": 8, "BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS": 40 }
```
sandeep: pushed patch to config-store for apac, TTL 5m. Also triggered cache-warm for hot prefixes.
taylor: also set KV_CACHE_TTL=300s and PREFIX_CACHE_WARM=on for top tenants.
jeff: applied. I see batch_size distribution drop from median 32 -> 6 in the collector stream.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback to v1.3.6 completed (global) at 15:04:10 UTC.
oncall-runner: verifying metrics — 15:06 checks:
- 99p latency apac-prod: 420ms -> 88ms
- kv_cache_hit: 34% -> 84%
- avg batch size: 28 -> 7
oncall-runner: all core traces show tail improving. marking incident as mitigated for now.
maya: good catch. note: any geopolitical/regulatory tenants pinned to apac cannot be moved to na1. For those, we should keep emergency small-batch + cache-warm until we can do an infra fix.
li: agreed. plan: (1) keep continuous batching off in apac for next 12 hrs, (2) schedule a controlled canary of the kernel-selection changes on a small dedicated pool, (3) provision 2-4 spare GPUs in apac on next capacity window.
taylor: cost note: cross-region shift for paid customers acceptable; avoid for free tiers. we'll add routing policy: route tenants with tag = "high-priority" -> na1 when apac degraded; others -> reduced model (gpt-lite)
jeff: leaving a few debug traces here for postmortem:
```
EPOCH 2026-07-09T15:01:23Z runtime: kernel-selector chose fused-attn-optim
trace: batch_size_observed=64 queue_delay_ms=1200 kv_evicts=+4532
```
maya: filing incident doc. can someone grab cost delta estimate for the NA shift? we need to include it in postmortem.
li: I’ll get a rough number — rough estimate: +$0.03/token egress for heavy sessions moved to NA1 due to inter-region.
taylor: thanks. next actions: keep apac continuous batching disabled, schedule kernel-selector canary on a tiny reserved pool, provision 2 GPUs in apac next maintenance, confirm rollback telemetry stable for 1 hour, and then update incident ticket.
jeff: noted. if any regression recurs, we escalate to SEVs.
maya: nice work team :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident-bot: incident #INC-2026-423 created, severity: S2, owners: eng-infra, eng-runtime.
oncall-runner: closing thread here, will add links to incident doc once it's up.
